title: More turns on a motor coil
hook: Change number of turns and predict magnetic torque magnitude.

doesNotKnow: torque magnitude = N I A B abs(sinθ)

misconception: magnetic torque magnitude stays fixed when number of turns doubles.
objective: Apply torque magnitude = N I A B abs(sinθ) to compare magnetic torque magnitude when number of turns changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an identical planar coil with fixed current area field and angle θ between the coil normal and the field, torque magnitude = N I A B abs(sinθ). When number of turns doubles, magnetic torque magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model torque magnitude = N I A B abs(sinθ); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an identical planar coil with fixed current area field and angle θ between the coil normal and the field, with a nonzero initial result. If number of turns triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnetic torque magnitude?
recall.why: Apply torque magnitude = N I A B abs(sinθ) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
